newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs slip from highs but still end firmer in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGBs slip from highs but still end firmer in Tokyo.

text.p: The benchmark September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract slipped from earlier highs by the end of Tokyo trade on Thursday, yet still managed to finish firmer, traders said.
Short-covering was the main factor behind the key contract's rise although some investor buying, thin market conditions and slightly improving sentiment all helped it gain.
Gains may have been trimmed by a late rise in Tokyo stocks, which ended up by 160.51, or 20,519.25, one trader said.
September ranged from 124.86 to 125.23 before falling back to close at 125.14. Volume was 31,476 contracts.
"If there had been investor buying, September would certainly have risen farther than it did, particularly as there was little in the way of selling going on," a trust bank trader said.

Other traders said that investor interest in bond buying was likely to pick up over the short term, perhaps pushing the key contract even higher. But they acknowledged that a rise over 126.00 appears to be highly unlikely for now.
Signs that the market seems to be absorbing last week's flood of corporate bond issues well also lent support to today's buying.
